rows: The compiler: a term to JS source (compile_full, try_compile), and its runtime, $R (structural equality, builtins, parameters and samples).

The boundary: Hazel values into JS (to_js) and back (of_js, read by the types the compiler recorded), a livelit definition compiled and its view and update called (view_of_def, call_view, call_update), and the counts and timings the Firefox check reads.
A slide's whole run, compiled, with each livelit's model a parameter (^report(49)).

Node, not a build of the app (^report(45))
The Witch's whole program (2,222 lines, 53 livelits), at each of four steps
An elaborated term to JS source, or the reason it does not compile. compile_full also gives the constructors' types and the functions, for the way back.
Runs the source as new Function("$R", src) with the runtime: the term's value, in JS.
A Hazel value into JS, and a JS value back into Hazel, read by the type expected where it sits.

A view's answer drawn straight from its JS, every form HazelDOM draws.

rows: Modules, to_fixed, and the Polygons slide's view compiled whole
Cheaper ids; a number written with a minus

The Witch's whole run compiled (command line), 76 to 127 times faster
Each livelit's model a parameter, so a step is a call with a new argument, not new code
At a livelit's event, the run draws every livelit; each livelit's view folded into the run, a macro livelit's too
A step back to a slider's starting value keeps the run's answers

columns: What it would take away, as measured on build 8
rows: Compile the program once, not again after a step that changed only a livelit's model: keep the compiled program, and give it the new models.
126 to 141 ms of the page's thread after each step.
Leave the worker out when the compiled run has answered: keep the run's answers when the worker catches up, and hold the worker's request until the steps stop.
The page drawing every livelit again from the worker's answer, to the same picture; the worker's run for each step of a quick series.
Send values as data where they cross: the worker's answer and its probe samples without ids, holes or closures.
The answer is 590 KB, encoded in 70 ms in the worker and decoded in 13 ms in the page; the Witch's picture is 3 times smaller as data (^report(47)).
started: the first slice, the samples' values on the way to the page (^ticket(718))
Draw only the livelits a drag changes: make the editors' and projectors' views incremental.
Most of the page's view, 10.1 ms of a 17.1 ms median frame of a drag.
Handle a slider's change event without an edit of the program, as cut A did for its input events, or do the edit's work after the paint.
Statics and syntax (32 ms) and the whole slide's view (91 ms), all before the paint at 176 ms.
